news.title: England Women in World Cup 2027 play-offs: Lionesses have obligation to prove themselves after Spain disappointment
news.lede: When England were consigned to the World Cup play-offs back in June, it felt like a massive step backwards. How were the European champions not a shoo-in for the next major tournament in the international calendar? The Lionesses only missed out by a whisker, finishing their qualifying campaign with 15 points from a possible 18. But it's difficult to overlook how we got here.

news.title: Albania v Wales: Rhian Wilkinson wants clean sheet in Women's World Cup play-off semi-final first leg
news.lede: Rhian Wilkinson led Wales to Euro 2025, the first women's major tournament in the nation's history. Rhian Wilkinson has identified a clean sheet as the first target for Wales in Friday's Women's World Cup play-off semi-final first leg against Albania. Wales face Albania at the 16,000-capacity Loro Borici Stadium in Shkoder before next Tuesday's return in Llanelli. Wilkinson's side beat their play-off opponents twice during the group stage of World Cup qualifying in April, when they followed up a 4-0 home victory with a scrappy 1-0 success on their travels.

news.title: Saudi Arabia appears to be shelving plans for its most ambitious World Cup stadium project. But why?
news.lede: Since winning the right to hold the 2034 World Cup unopposed, Saudi Arabia has been pulling away from sport. With reports that its most ambitious stadium project will be abandoned, what does this mean for the World Cup? It was billed as "the most unique stadium in the world," a key pillar of Saudi Arabia's World Cup 2034 plans. But now Neom Stadium, part of the kingdom's ambitious aims to build a 170-kilometer-long (111miles) city in the desert known as The Line, looks set to be scrapped, with the broader project scaled back significantly.

news.title: Women’s World Cup Brazil 2027: Countdown and Latest Updates
news.lede: The road to the FIFA Women’s World Cup Brazil 2027 is gathering momentum. For the first time, South America will host the world’s biggest women’s football tournament, placing Brazil at the centre of a historic moment for the game. In our monthly countdown, we’ll follow the key developments shaping the tournament and its wider impact on women’s football, bringing you stories and insights from Brazil and beyond through the perspective of our exclusive correspondent in Brazil, Elena Mueller. The tournament will take place from 24 June to 25 July 2027 across eight Host Cities, with 32 national teams competing in 64 matches.

news.title: “The World Cup Has Come and Gone” — Friday Ekpo Dismisses DR Congo Speculation, Demands Evidence of Nigeria’s FIFA Protest
news.lede: Former Super Eagles midfielder Friday Ekpo has urged Nigerians to stop relying on speculation surrounding DR Congo’s alleged use of an ineligible player during the 2026 FIFA World Cup qualification process, insisting that only documentary evidence of an official protest can establish grounds for further action. news.title: Czech Republic vs Scotland LIVE: Women's World Cup qualifying - BBC Alba coverage, live text & report
news.lede: Erin Cuthbert has not played since opening the scoring for Scotland against Israel on 5 June. Chelsea captain Erin Cuthbert is available for Scotland's Women's World Cup round one two-legged play-off against the Czech Republic despite not featuring for her club this season. The midfielder, who was announced as skipper of the Women's Super League club last month, has not featured for Sonia Bompastor's side as she recovers from a knee injury sustained on international duty in June. But the 28-year-old has meticulously followed the plan agreed between her club and Scotland, so is in contention to make her first appearance of the season when Melissa Andreatta's side face the Czech Republic in Pardubice on Friday evening - live on the BBC.

news.title: Nations League in Review: Thomas Tuchel’s Post-World Cup England
news.lede: After a miserable World Cup semi-final exit this summer, Thomas Tuchel’s popularity as England boss was at its lowest since his tenure began officially in January 2025. A defeat to the world champions aside, England’s first four fixtures of their UEFA Nations League campaign have breathed new life into the tenure of the Three Lions boss. Following their narrow 3-2 defeat to La Roja, Tuchel’s side have netted 12 goals without reply in their following three games. A professional performance in Prague, followed by a dismantling of Croatia behind closed doors, rounded off with a comfortable victory over Czechia in the return fixture at Wembley has seen the faith well and truly restored in Tuchel’s position as England manager.
